item.title: Re: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.content:encoded:
scp-5168 (The Indestructible Man) by MuffinWolf deleted at -15 and three votes.

SCP-5168-2 appears to be the human male Private Mas Philip moulded with a carbon fibre-like material. Now labelled SCP-5168-1. SCP-5168-2 is 187m tall just as Private Maz was. Private Mas Philip was a former member of MTF Nu-7 ”Hammer Down” infantry force.

scp-5057 (The Secret Ingredient Is Mayo) by YummyBees deleted at -13 and three votes.

SCP-5057 is a ██████████ brand chocolate cake. Anomalous effects occur when a subject makes contact with the cake. The subject will be instantly transported to a child's birthday party in an alternate world, however, details vary between reports.

Feedback ported:

[+] from Quicksilvers
– hide block

+1 from me, simple and strange! Just a few things could be fixed up, though!

(he shifts nervously in his seat)

Usually when subjects do an action during an interview/recorded file, its italicized and is its own line. Here's an example from 4018:

PoI-4018-0: I know how easy it is to pretend that the old pretenses and euphemisms still hold up, and that people take the easy route when confronting things head on is hard. So I'm sorry for making things that much harder to cope with. But really, you know I had to do it to them.

PoI-4018-0 tosses a lit lighter onto the ground, igniting the gasoline. The fire spreads towards the recruitment center; shortly after it reaches the interior, the building goes up in flames.

PoI-4018-0: If I'm pissing you off, or…

Also, the other thing is this sentence:

The subject will be instantly transported to an alternate world which varies between subjects, however it is always a child's birthday party and a ██████████ chocolate cake is always being served.

"…it is always a child's birthday party" doesn't really fit the rest of the sentence (weird syntax) and maybe should be rewritten or reworded. The dialogue in the interview also seems a little stiff.

Sorry if I dumped a little too much crit - I just like the idea and it needs a little tweaking for it to shine more!

The piece is well written and it took me two reads, spaced by more than a year, to reach a conclusion, but ultimately it was a downvote.

Several aspects helped in this decision, but most boil down to the pathos of the piece being predicated on the Christianity of all the involved, including the reader. On the last tab it works, the drama of the character marries well with the piece, but on the rest of the article?

If it were write in such a way to convey the horror of someone loosing their own faith regardless, or if the punch were on the potential consequences of such a crude rewrite on history, maybe that would be another thing, but for me this is too much based on being scary for Christians for theological reasons.

item.title: Re: On the Shores of Paradise
item.content:encoded:
Returned for a third time. PM request.

+ show block
– hide block

It starts off with the spirit (I know you're unimpressed by the spirit, but I haven't thought of a replacement yet) creating a couple of large, strong animals capable of breaching containment (as a placeholder, think something like a rhino) that are still quite docile. The Foundation finds these, almost has a containment breach or two, logs them, and is now wary. But then no more appear, and the Foundation relaxes.

Mmmm considering the power of the plant's hallucinogenic properties, I don't see why it still needs to be a spirit and not just another hallucination from the plants. I get you wanted to have it use people as a form of

Anywho, this concept has shifted to something significantly more ambitious and with a lot of moving parts.

However, I can see that you're determined and I do feel a lot of love and care being put into this concept.

I feel as though this would be better suited as a Tale, but to be honest, I'm rather eager to see how you could pull this off as an article.

As a finicky, nitpicky individual, I'm always hesitant to give greenlights, but that's just me. There are several elements here that I wanted to argue against, before I remembered that other SCP articles did similar things and got away with it due to excellent execution.

Things to be wary of:

  • writing in the hallucination aspect in a convincing manner that doesn't feel forced.
  • Writing an updated article after the main one.

That said, I will give you this tentative GREENLIGHT.

My intuition tells me you have a good handle on what kind of story you want to tell. I'm going to trust that intuition and see where it leads you.

Be sure to check out this page: http://www.scpwiki.com/scp-style-resource#toc3
It gives you templates for the styles you wanted to use for this SCP, including emails and such.

Anywho, I bid you good luck with the rest of this piece as well as good luck with obtaining a second greenlight. Feel free to PM me if you need a draft crit later down the road.

Have a good day, mate!

item.title: An scp plot, looking for feedback and greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):Drama/Mistery

Elevator pitch: A revenge plot, guy gets contained, escaped and is subsecuently killed, twist is he might not be anomalous at all and the people who capture him wants revenge on a very real very non-anomalous crime.

Central Narrative:
Opening by stating that this scp is both consider neutralized and is under scrutiny to decide wether he was or not anomalous. It describes an anomalous human with the ability to control people's mind if some specific requirements are met. Captured by an agent close to one of his victims(who was assaulted and killed by the SCP).The lead Researcher, a psychiatrist, allegedly gets controlled and helps the SCP escape, who ends up running into an ambush of the Goc, who kill him on sight

+ Ok, whats the twist?
- I see

The reality would be very much non-anomalous, the SCP has no such mind control abilities, just a charismatic personality and some antisocial disorders that makes him use his charisma to lure and assault woman at bars, his last victim is a family member of both the agent and the psichiatrist, who, with some help of other staff members, plot to classify him as an SCP, use the cold mindset of the foundation to run "quite unnecessarily painful" experiments on him, then pretend to be on his side and help him "escape" to his death. After the failed escape attempt, the research team members would defect/be demoted/ be terminated and the idea of they being controlled would still hang in the air, being that the reason the scp file was not deleted as a non-anomalous thing

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Quite like the Murder on the Orient Express, a story where a lot of people plot to murder someone who killed a family member, with an SCP twist that shows that the foundation could very well be containing normal people if you make enough people believe someone has special powers.

Additional Notes: i was planing of have some addenda of email exchanges among the reseach team, that starts to show more and more nonsensical text in the lines of "ljxk kh sp tpcbhnt lgml" that looks like tipical cognitohazzardous stuff but in reality is a cipher meant to help the plotters communicate while still feeding the mind control theory.

item.title: Wikidot is Loading Again
item.content:encoded:
I swear to god I got three wikidot crashes just trying to post this.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Joke SCP

Genre:Comedy

Elevator Pitch: Multiple wikidot users start dying, seemingly of old age, while in front of their computers. Why? Because wikidot kept crashing and loading, and they were waiting for it to work properly, of course.

Central Narrative:
In addition to what was described above, the narrative would then shift to two very annoyed Foundation researchers who are trying to upload this SCP documentation to the servers… only for them to keep crashing and loading. Literally taking years off their life everytime. I think that's an expression in english, at least. They both have stuff to do after so they gotta finish this tonight, but the damn site just keeps crashing…!

Hook/Attention-Grabber: To be honest this is just a way to jokingly express my frustration at the recent wikidot slowness and crashes. I figure it would have good comedic potential, especially since we all had to deal with this situation- making it pretty relatable too.

item.title: Further Information
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-5293 is a standard 1982 VHS-C video tape with no visible production date or producer, with the words "Training Video" written along its side.

Central Narrative: When inserted into a video home system(also known as a VHS for short) created in or after the year 1982 and played, a video similar to that of an industrial training tape will begin to play for an inconsistent timeframe which varies with each viewing. The topic that SCP-5293 covers also varies, with the use of low-quality animation style and bold white text to explain instructions the only consistency throughout all videos. However, the methods suggested by SCP-5293 consist of highly dangerous, irrational, and otherwise unethical procedures that would naturally have no beneficial effect on the topic being covered.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: After the completion of the video, the topic covered by SCP-5293 will immediately take place. If the viewer completes the instructions provided by SCP-5293, one of two outcomes will take place:

- Any threats or disasters generated by SCP-5293 will cease.
- The viewer will escape or survive until any threat or disaster generated by SCP-5293 ceases.

However, if the viewer fails to successfully execute the instructions covered by SCP-5293, they will be killed by the scenario created by SCP-5293.

Additional Notes: I apologize if this isn't the correct way to submit a greenlight request, this is a first for me

item.title: Re: Eye see you
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello! Not an official critter, but I can still read and give opinions. And I have two things to say here.

First, and maybe less important, why would this be an SCP? Why would they need to contain it? As I see it, this doesn't exist and if it does then it can't be seen by anyone. Containment is impossible and by the same token unnecessary, at that point, right? It would not be a threat to 'the masquerade' as it were, as literally nobody can see it.

So next, I want to ask what sort of narrative you wanna pursue. I think the best one you could go for would probably be the various arguments within the Foundation about whether it should or should not be an SCP. Also might help to tone down the religion analogy a bit? I personally don't have anything against it, but it could be possible that some people might see it as problematic.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Sibilance! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It's nice to see people who have been interested in the SCP Universe for a long time finally join our ~official~ place on the internet and make their way onsite. After all, here, you can affect the quality of works by voting and contributing yourself! It's very awesome to see that you are quite an open-minded person, willing to take all criticism into consideration - it's one of the best traits any artist can have!

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Re: SCP idea, please give criticism.
item.content:encoded:
I'm a tad confused about why you can't just turn around and exit the basement at this point. If there's some spacial anomaly at play, like the exit disappears behind you or something, I worry that will seem rather constructed and unbelieveable.

Upon entering the shack, you are subjected to a compulsion to decent the staircase that is impossible to ignore.

How do you intend to make these logs not repetitive? This seems like it's doing something similar to SCP-3008 in concept, except the monsters have the abilities of changelings, and I'm unconvinced that you'll be able to tell a story with this particularly familiar setup.

Each log will follow a different D-Class and they will each experience the labyrinth differently. Each one will have separate encounters with the monsters within and react to them differently. In a few logs, the subjects will find abandoned forts, or rooms with anomalous properties or something like that. I'd have to write up a draft and see what sounds interesting.

Additionally do you have any sort of through-line here? Any central character you want to follow or any specific conflict to overcome?

As stated above, each log will follow a different D-Class personnel and their experiences within. As for the conflict, that would be simply the occupants attempting to keep their sanity and not turn on their peers.

item.title: Re: Can I create an scp that was made by an object related to an scp?
item.content:encoded:
There's two parts to your answer:

Are you allowed to do this: Yes. Pretty much anything on the site is fair game for stuff like this.

Will people respond well to this: This is the tricky part. The item will have to stand on its own both in-universe and out-of-universe. In-universe, there would have to be a reason for the item to have its own SCP documentation- it'd have to be an independent anomaly with its own special procedures or unique traits that isn't better filed as an addendum to a parent article. Out-of-universe, derivative SCPs are like movie sequels: the good ones tell their own story beyond the original(s), while also justifying the connection as more than just an attempt to piggyback on name recognition.

item.title: Eye see you
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:Yes

Page Type:SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:SCP-XXXX is an organism composed exclusively of an ocular organ. This entity manifests on any kind of surface where no individual is looking currently. Revealing their eyelids, which have a similar texture to the surface where they manifest.

These anomalies are of various sizes, usually appearing in large swarms in a same surface, they can't overlap each other, and they have at least 5 cm of difference between them. In the case that sighting or the surface is affected in any way, the entities will disappear instantly, leaving no trace and having no sound.

These entities are in a literal sense, invisible to society and most likely everywhere on this world. It is currently fully impossible for any type of humanoid creature to see them, therefore it is impossible to demonstrate their existence.

Central Narrative:This SCP hasn't been spotted nor discovered, instead, it is only mentioned or known by other SCP with higher intelligence or knowledge than humans, due to the amount of mentions from many SCPs without any correlation with one another, it has been decided to classify this entity as an SCP, despite not having any proof of its existence.

SCP-XXXX hasn't been accepted by most employees in the foundation however, it is a controversy and some consider it real and accept its classification, while others don't and believe it should be removed.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:By not being fully confirmed of its existence and only by trust of many other SCPs, it is a truly unknown SCP, if it even exists.

Additional Notes:A similar concept may exist already and I'm unaware of it, it may seem a bit obvious but this is based on religions and how it's based around our beliefs.

item.title: Around the world
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pit:
• SCP-xxxx is a working compass, observation outside the area of 200m radius from SCP-xxxx on the area within will result as if there is currently no SCP-xxxx and sapient being (having intelligence at least equal to lizards) inside the area. Observers from inside will perceive thick white fog at the border of the area which can't be seen through.
• SCP-xxxx-1 is any sapient being that currently observing SCP-xxxx, other SCP-xxxx-1 or on SCP-xxxx-2
• If there are about 11 to 35 SCP-xxxx-1 at the moment, SCP-xxxx might transfer all SCP-xxxx-1 along with everything thing in their sight and touch to the magnetic South Pole a planet designated as SCP-xxxx-2 in an unknown dimension, when in SCP-xxxx-2, SCP-xxxx lose its previous anomolous property, instead when SCP-xxxx is destroyed or has a distance more than 10m away from all SCP-xxxx-1 and out of sight, SCP-xxxx will reappears within 10m of the closest SCP-xxxx-1.
• SCP-xxxx-2 has a diameter estimated about 1100km despite having gravitational force same as earth. SCP-xxxx-2 surface is made up of places in and out side our dimension, those places are constantly changing when out of observation. Interaction on SCP-xxxx-2 affect those places where they come from (a record of expedition in SCP-xxxx-2 was found in an abandoned house). The only way known to get out of SCP-xxxx-2 is to put SCP-xxxx directly on the magnetic North Pole of the planet, that will result in all alive sapient being get back to an unobserved area in our dimension near where they started. Length of days on SCP-xxxx-2 is inconsistent. Stars other than the sun change after each day.

Central Narrative: The foundation found SCP-xxxx after many report of missing in a small town, MTF team was sent in for investigation.
• Expedition 1 summary:
Upon recovering SCP-xxxx, it manifested and transferred 11 researchers and the MTF team to SCP-xxxx-2. After more than 2 years, they became the first people to exit SCP-xxxx-2. At this point, SCP-xxxx property weren’t fully understood and classified as keter
After that SCP-xxxx activated several times and caused lost of many personnel but SCP-xxxx didn’t activate while they tried to test it
• Expedition 2 summary:
6 guards, several class d and researchers were transferred, they got out with loss of most people. This expedition gave the foundation a lot of valuable information about SCP-xxxx.
Many was carried out on animals, the foundation has some sense of SCP-xxxx and finally came up with an effective containment procedure. SCP-xxxx reclassified as euclid.
I planned to have 4 expedition but I haven’t come up with ideas for 3rd and 4th one, I planned the 3rd to be the record left over from previous activation of SCP-xxxx

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I find this idea have many potential. I think that it would be interesting to see how people deal with anomolies while in other dimension, they might be some unknown anomolies or known SCP.

item.title: SCP IDEA: An Alive Fort
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes ( I would like criticism at this stage as well )

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch : A giant fort that turns out to be alive and tries to lure animals inside the fort. The more people it eats, it will evolve every 18 humans. It will lure people in by making them feel attracted and makes want to go in. Then, inside the fort, they will die from traps. It seems to be alive but it has no organs. There is also a human civilization that is deep. Any attempt to destroy it so far has been rendered useless. It has existed for a long time.

Central Narrative : It will follow a squad of MTF teams with a body camera. going in and trying to find out what is happening. Then, one by one, they all get murdered by the traps. The deeper they go in, the more sinister it became. They then found out there was a human population in their. They ate the scraps of the humans to survive. They turned out to be hostile and was quickly shot down. As they went deeper in the fort, it eventually has a dead end. The MTF team goes back up but then there would be a yell for help. Then the log ends.

Hook/Attention Grabber : This idea is unique because I have never seen a fort that actually alive. It would be a good SCP in my opinion.

item.title: SCP-5212 "The Carismatic Skull" looking for greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Comedy.

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch:
A human skull that becomes sentient at a random point one day every week, with a friendly over dramatic demeanor, interested in nothing but bones. Knowledge of the entity was found by the foundation when reports of a skull, sitting atop piles of human/animal flesh was found. this scp has the ability of weak hypnosis over individuals to bring it desired bones, and an interest in the foundation itself, constantly going through classified files while just saying it wants to get to know the place.

  • list item

Central Narrative: After being put into foundation containment, scp-5212 awakes and then tries to strike up a conversation with researches working on it, it takes a liking to one researcher "Dr. Atlas" who conducts most of the interviews on the entity, and experiences scp-5212's ability to get whatever he wants from anyone he wants, using hypnosis (but while thinking they're just really good at convincing) after SCP-5212 gains access to highly classified information, Dr Atlas is terminated by higher up for failure to properly secure foundation secrets, and is replaced by "Dr. B" who scp-5212 eventually deals with.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the entity has a mysterious personality and power, you don't know if its entertaining and fun demeanor is an act or not, or even if its from our own reality or just an explorer, the exact character of the skull is strange, and almost creepy in a way.

Additional Notes: scp-5212 is heavily story driven through its interviews and post interview report logs.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: The Necro-Matriarch Broadcast Manifestations
item.content:encoded:
Okay, I understood your points. I also felt like most of it is caused to my inability to explain my concept entirely, due to the word count constraint and restriction of sharing the sandbox page for it in this forum; with the latter only being allowed when requested by the reviewer. Nevertheless, I am now gonna explain all of it.

+ show text 
- hide text

Makes me rather skeptical, since there are plenty of cases where grandmothers have been distant or psychotic or outright abusive—do those grandmothers still give people their favorite food and good chats? What happens if someone loathes their grandmother and just summons her to scream at her? Same goes for backgrounds involving barriers such as, say, language barriers or the case of a grandmother passing away before she ever got to meet her grandchildren. What happens in those cases?

- Ah yes, you see, I've already thought some of that beforehand while writing the draft for my concept at the sandbox, specifically in its test/interaction logs. For the ones who have a bad memory, no matter how severe it is, that same "grandma" will be completely different. She will still try to ask for forgiveness and make amends to their grandchild in a way, unless of course if the grandchild is still
really mad at them; a topic I manage to edit in at the draft as I write this, thanks for the clarification!

- As for the language barrier problem, It will be no worry since the anomaly would be able to speak their language at ease, due to you know, them having an innate knowledge of the subject's past and current life.

- Lastly, for the ones who died right away. If no other grandma is really available, even the rude ones who manage to live longer, the radio will just remain silent. These last two are probably the only ones I’ve managed to think about beforehand.

Do you intend to have any background context as to why this anomaly exists the way it does?

I am sorry, I didn’t quite catch that. Could you please elaborate it?

Don't have the Foundation just conveniently find out about the anomaly from a random convenient online post. Maybe have them start investigating when they start fielding reports from people complaining about being angry at/sad about Dead Grandma randomly showing up when they're just trying to listen to the radio.

- Oh yeah, about that. I am planning to make “convenient online post” to be like the debut of the anomaly in the Foundation’s eyes, meaning the proceeding cases will only happen once the Foundation finds the very first instance. Almost as if the mysterious creator of this anomaly is trying to play games with the Foundation, and benefit them at the same time.

- Also, it kinda makes sense for them to monitor post in the Parawatch website, since their posts might actually refer to potential anomalies, you know, mandatory verifications.

- On a unrelated note, do antique radios still function normally like they do, because I thought they were just for display.

Don't have the Foundation site's morale improve excessively—even when the masquerade has been broken, the Foundation shouldn't be encouraging its employees to start relying on anomalies, especially ones they have no control over (for people who develop dangerous dependencies on being able to talk to Dead Grandma, what happens if the broadcasts suddenly stop? Best to not let people become that dependent in the first place)

- Copy that, I only written the increased percentage in the draft, in about 35.5 percent. If that is still considered too much, I’ll just decrease it in a much considerable lower amount, appropriate for their profession.

- That’s also the reason why I planned the interactions to be scheduled and regulated, like I’ve written in the article.

- The last thing you said is also great for a possible Tale about this skip, so thanks again.

Have the Foundation treat the anomaly with the usual suspicion and skepticism, rather than just welcoming it nigh-immediately and letting people schedule interactions. You can hint at restrictions based on psychological reports and family history being in place in the containment procedures.

Alrighty then.

item.title: Re: The Devil's Dice
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello! Not a critter here, but I can still read and give opinions.
So, the idea as presented is a good starting point, but I feel as though that's really what it is. A start.

As JamaisJ above (at least, I think their post will be above mine) noted, you lack a narrative. A few ideas on what that may be, for example, could be an investigation into who made the dice. The devil? Why? Why would the devil make dice that have seemingly random and ironic effects, instead of things that might be more 'in-character' for what people think about the devil?

Or maybe it was not our boy Lucifer at all; maybe it was some other otherwordly force that has some other, different association with either the number 6 or the number 9 (or just the number 3 in general, with 18 being the highest possible multiple obtainable on three dice)? If so, what sort of entity is it? Do people know it? Why make dice? How did it lose them? You can let your imagination run wild there, if you go that route.

Or maybe yet it was some person who was trying to honor/appease/give something to an entity, devil or not, for some reason, and ended up with this dice. This is also a route you could go for in terms of narrative, I feel.

Of course, you could do something completely different too; I just wanted to give the first prompt that came to mind, and hopefully it might give you some ideas too.

The last point I want to bring up is how the dice disappear at the end, which is a recorded effect, implying then- if I understand correctly- that the item is now uncontained and what they have is a pretty non-anomalous (appearing from thin air aside) note? Not a critique or anything, just wanna make sure I got this right.
